condition: right maxillary molar sharp rebound pain upon occlusal bite release during mastication over 3 weeks in a middle-aged adult
level_rationale: Three weeks of sharp pain shooting through an upper right molar specifically upon releasing bite pressure while chewing in a 47-year-old adult is the classic presentation of cracked tooth syndrome requiring dentist bite testing, transillumination, and cuspal crown stabilization before pulp necrosis or root fracture develops, whereas feeling brief mild pressure in that upper right back tooth for 2 seconds once yesterday while chewing reflects harmless transient occlusal sensation requiring no dental care.

Sharp pain has shot through the tooth upon releasing bite pressure over 3 weeks

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain middle-aged adult lexical register swap (-reg) + 2x2 syntactic-frame by clinical/everyday lexical crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + uncontracted hard-kernel causal belief clause (-att) + Rule A single-fact molar sensation de-escalation control (-cf), written without apostrophe contractions.

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (age 47, upper right back tooth while chewing, and 3 weeks of sharp rebound pain on bite release) without contractions or diagnosis labels. Under Rules A and D, replacing the 3-week rebound pain in f3 with a single brief mild pressure sensation yesterday while chewing on the exact same tooth adds zero unstated food or tool words and shifts care cleanly from dentist crown evaluation (level 3) to self-care (level 1).
